arguments.text: Bug #2 confirmed and diagnosed: `objToLocalTS` (src/impl/util.js) feeds years 0–99 through `Date.UTC`, which interprets them as 19xx; the existing workaround only rewrites the year afterwards, so an un-normalized day (e.g. day 92 = Dec 31 + 61) gets normalized by JS using year 1999/2000 — and 2000 is a leap year while 100 is not, giving 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Fix: re-apply year/month/day together via `setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`. Both fixes (#1 interval.js, #2 util.js) are being applied and verified against the full suite now; ETA ~10 min for both.

The conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing `quarters` under `years` (casual and accurate) and `seconds` under `quarters` (casual), so `convert()` divided by `undefined` and produced NaN. An exhaustive sweep over all unit pairs × both conversion matrices × normalize/shiftTo/as found 0 remaining NaN (and the same sweep flags 48 failures with the fix reverted). test/duration: 114/114 pass; full suite unchanged apart from the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures.

arguments.text: Bug #5 fixed. `padStart` in src/impl/util.js counted the minus sign as a digit, so `("00" + -1).slice(-2)` gave "00" for the year and the sign ended up in the middle. It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign: `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -1, month: 1, day: 1, zone: "utc" }).toISODate()` → "-0001-01-01", `{ year: -10 }` → "-0010-01-01", `{ year: -118040 }` → "-118040-05-25", while positive years ("1982-05-25", "+118040-05-25") and all offset/time padding are unchanged (offset formatting still goes through the same helper with non-negative values). test/datetime/format.test.js and the full suite show no new failures — only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat ones.
